result:
Decode attention is memory-bound, so time is roughly the KV cache bytes read divided by the achievable HBM bandwidth.

KV bytes: 64 seqs × 16384 tokens × 8 KV heads × 128 dim × 2 (K and V) × 2 bytes (BF16) = 64 × 16384 × 4096 B = 4.295 GB (about 4.29e9 bytes).

B300 HBM3e peak is about 8 TB/s. FlashAttention split-KV decode typically reaches about 80–85% of peak, so about 6.5–6.8 TB/s effective. At about 6.6 TB/s, the KV read takes about 650 µs.

The combine kernel is small: it reads partial outputs and LSEs, and adds a few µs, plus launch overhead. Q and O traffic are negligible.

Total is roughly 650 + 8 ≈ 660 µs.
